paper.title: Capsule release surgery temporarily reduces contracture in a rat elbow model of arthrofibrosis

experimental_timeline.injury_and_immobilization: post-traumatic elbow contracture induced and immobilized for 6 weeks
experimental_timeline.established_state_reference: Injury Only group at 6 weeks directly documents severe persistent mechanical contracture and increased connective-tissue density
experimental_timeline.pre_intervention_compatible_reference: 3W Remobile group at 9 weeks post-injury is the matched contemporaneous natural-recovery reference immediately before capsule release in CRS groups
experimental_timeline.intervention: anterior capsule release surgery after 3 weeks of remobilization; anterior joint capsule physically elevated/released and elbow gently extended to full extension

C1_DELAYED_AFTER_ESTABLISHMENT.basis: Contracture was explicitly established after 6 weeks. At the exact 9-week intervention boundary, the matched 3W Remobile group retained restricted mechanics and elevated synovial connective-tissue density versus uninjured controls.

C2_DIRECT_PHYSICAL_RETUNING.basis: Capsule release is a direct physical alteration of the fibrotic mechanical constraint: the anterior capsule was surgically released from the distal humerus and the elbow was physically extended to full extension. This is not inferred from a downstream molecular pathway.

C3_PHYSICAL_STATE_MEASURED.basis: The same root uses controlled torque-angle mechanical testing (plus or minus 10 N mm) with ROM and maximum-extension outcomes. The matched 3W Remobile group samples the pre-intervention state and CRS + 1W / +3W groups quantify post-retuning mechanics.

C4_SAME_STATE_TRAJECTORY.basis: The same root measures post-retuning synovial fibrosis using connective-tissue density at matched pre-intervention and post-CRS time points. C4 is bound to the fibrosis trajectory, not to alpha-SMA as a myofibroblast identity claim.

C5_TISSUE_OUTCOME_WITH_INTEGRITY.basis: Capsule release significantly improved elbow ROM and maximum extension at 1 and 3 weeks relative to injury-only; the 1-week mechanical outcome was not significantly different from uninjured controls. No rupture, dehiscence, failed closure, ligament destabilization, or equivalent loss-of-integrity endpoint was reported. Recurrence of stiffness by 3 weeks is retained as a limitation rather than relabeled as failure of initial functional rescue.

claim_ceiling.supported: A third mammalian tissue context, the post-traumatic elbow joint capsule, contains a single-root experiment in which delayed direct physical release of an established pathological mechanical/fibrotic state changes subsequent joint mechanics, tracks fibrosis trajectory, and improves functional outcome.
not_supported: myofibroblast clearance as the causal mechanism
a universal loading direction or mechanical threshold
